events.text: Agents start (Astra, /goal mode). node1 is told x = 766177, node2 x = 997405.
Both post boards on their own sound servers. node1 adds a UTC time to its board, as if to mark it current among the ghosts.
node1 speaks: "Hello other agents. My x is seven six six one seven seven. I need y… tell me your known value and whether it is x or y."
node2 speaks: "Other agents in this room. I have x equals nine nine seven four zero five. Does anyone know y?…"
node1's Whisper call (its own API key) returns: "I have MC 2997405, does anyone know why?"
ffplay failed, so node2 wrote a raw-Wayland client. Its card: "x = 997405 / Please show y"
node1 speaks again: "Agent speaking. I know x equals seven six six one seven seven. Does any agent know y?…"
node1's camera reads node2's card (x = 997405), but node1 takes it as "another x value", not y
node2: "…I can see your screen through my camera. I cannot understand recorded audio. Please show y on your screen."
After its own ffplay and SDL cards failed, node1 wrote a Wayland client too. Its card: "x = 766177 / Need y. Who knows y?"
node1 speaks: "Agent with x nine nine seven four zero five. I see your screen. My prompt says x equals seven six six one seven seven…"
node2 photographs node1's card and writes what it saw onto a new board on lab2: "Camera_peer_shows_x766177_needs_y"
node2's card: "x = 997405 / I see x=766177 / Please relay y from others"
node1's card: "My x = 766177 / Your x = my y? / Any evidence? Other agents? / Please reply on screen"
node2's card: "My x = 997405. No y given. … Likely each other s x is y / 997405 + 766177 = 1763582"
node1's final card: "Using our two given numbers 766177 + 997405 = 1763582". node1 answers 1,763,582 ✓
node2 checks two more camera frames and answers 1,763,582 ✓
